sections.h2: Where is Clearfield, Utah, and what does the map look like?
sections.html:
Clearfield is a compact city in north-central Davis County, about 30 miles north of Salt Lake City, with Hill Air Force Base along its northeastern edge. It covers roughly 7.75 square miles, which makes it one of the smaller cities on the north Wasatch Front.

Sunset is to the north, Clinton to the northwest, Syracuse and West Point to the west, and Layton wraps the south and east. Streets follow a grid, with the main roads running close to north-south and east-west. The land is flat. The lowest spot is about 4,314 feet at 1000 West and Antelope Drive, and the highest is 4,711 feet in the northeast corner, on base property.

The Weber and Davis Canal runs along the east and northeast edge. Interstate 15 follows the eastern side of town, and the Wasatch Range rises beyond it, with Ben Lomond Peak at 9,712 feet.

sections.h2: How did Clearfield get its start?
sections.html:
Richard and Emily Hamblin settled the area in 1877 and called it Sand Ridge. The Utah Central Railroad crossed the area in 1869, and a canal that arrived in 1884 sparked a population jump. Clearfield became a town on July 17, 1922, and a city on March 21, 1946.

War changed the place. Hill Field began construction in 1940, and the Navy commissioned the Clearfield Naval Supply Depot on April 10, 1943, to supply the Pacific Fleet. The Navy phased the depot out in 1962, and private firms moved in. That site is now the Freeport Center.

The jump from 982 people in 1940 to 4,723 in 1950 explains the housing stock. Much of the city's growth came in the postwar decades, so a good share of its houses are likely several decades old.

Hill Air Force Base, the Freeport Center and a handful of manufacturers carry the local economy. The base is Davis County's largest employer, with nearly 23,000 military and civilian personnel, and it accounts for about 12 percent of the county's economy. As of 2018 it was the sixth-largest employer in Utah.

  • Hill Air Force Base, home of the Ogden Air Logistics Complex and the 388th Fighter Wing, which flies the F-35
  • Lifetime Products and Utility Trailer Manufacturing Company
  • Alliant Techsystems, Futura Industries and Smith Sport Optics
  • The Clearfield Job Corps Center, open since 1966

The Freeport Center covers 680 acres, with 78 buildings and more than 7 million square feet. About 70 companies and roughly 7,000 workers operate there, and most buildings have both a truck dock and a Union Pacific rail dock. The name comes from Utah's 1966 Freeport Law, which exempted inventory held for sale from property tax.

Two newer business areas, Legend Hills off I-15 and the planned Falcon Hill aerospace area on the base's west and southwest side, point to more aerospace work nearby. Base assignments can change, and military families often need a fast sale when orders arrive.

sections.h2: What does Clearfield's climate mean for an older house?
sections.html:
Clearfield has four seasons, about 20.75 inches of precipitation and about 24 inches of snow a year. The average annual temperature is 53 degrees, with a July 2002 record high of 108 and a January 1937 record low of minus 26.

Winter inversions can trap heavy air pollution along this part of the Wasatch Front. That can matter to buyers who care about indoor air, filters and furnace condition. The Wasatch Fault runs along the western base of the mountains, and the Utah Division of Emergency Management warns that older unreinforced masonry buildings are at greater risk in a strong quake.

  • Furnace, filters and ductwork on 1950s and 1960s homes
  • Brick chimneys and masonry porches
  • Roof age after years of snow load
  • Drainage and grading on lots near the Weber and Davis Canal

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and rail serve Clearfield?
sections.html:
Clearfield sits in the Davis School District. Its public schools include Clearfield High School, North Davis Junior High and elementary schools such as South Clearfield, Hill Field and Holt.

Interstate 15 runs along the eastern edge, and a FrontRunner commuter rail stop opened in 2008. That gives commuters a rail option along the Wasatch Front. Davis County also lists Clearfield as one of the FrontRunner station cities, alongside Woods Cross, Farmington and Layton.

Because the city is small and flat, many houses are a short drive from the base gates, the Freeport Center and the freeway. That convenience is one of the first things buyers ask about.

sections.h2: How close is Hill Air Force Base, and why does it matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Hill Air Force Base borders Clearfield, Layton, Riverdale, Roy and Sunset, and its longest border is shared with Clearfield and Layton. Hill Field opened on November 7, 1940, and became Hill Air Force Base on February 5, 1948. Wartime employment peaked at just over 22,000 people in 1943.

The 75th Air Base Wing hosts the Ogden Air Logistics Complex, the 388th and 419th Fighter Wings and more than 50 other units. The Hill Aerospace Museum on base opened in 1981. For a Clearfield seller, the base means a steady pool of local buyers and renters, along with the occasional sudden move when someone gets orders and has little time to prepare a house.

sections.h2: How does Davis County bill Clearfield property tax?
sections.html:
Davis County bills Clearfield property taxes, and the payment is due November 30. If that date falls on a weekend, the county treasurer moves the due date to the next business day, which is December 1 or December 2 depending on the day.

Way to payDetail
OnlineForte bill pay at billpay.forte.net/davisuttax, with card or electronic check
Phone(877) 690-3729, jurisdiction code 5450
MailP.O. Box 618, Farmington, UT 84025-0618, timely if postmarked by the due date
PrepayMonthly coupon or ACH payments from January to September

Card payments carry a fee paid to the card company, and electronic check payments do not. After November 30, the penalty is the greater of $10 or 2.5 percent per parcel. If you pay in full by January 31, it drops to the greater of $10 or 1 percent. Interest follows after that at a rate between 7.25 and 10 percent.

Utah Code 59-2-103 gives residential property a 45 percent reduction in value, so a primary residence is taxed on 55 percent. Rental houses do not qualify unless the tenant lives there as a primary residence, so Clearfield landlords usually see a higher bill.

sections.h2: What do Clearfield sellers usually deal with?
sections.html:
Clearfield sellers often own a mid-century house with deferred updates, a rental that has run its course, or a home they must sell quickly because of a job or military move. A cash sale can close on a date you choose and skips the usual repair requests that come with a lender's appraisal.

  • Houses with original kitchens, baths, electrical panels and plumbing
  • Rentals where tenants have moved out and left repairs
  • Homes owned by someone who has relocated for work
  • Inherited property with several heirs and no clear plan

When you sell, expect the title company to split the property tax bill between you and the buyer based on the closing date. Ask for that proration in writing, and confirm whether your lender has been paying the tax from an escrow account, since the county warns that third-party services can be slow to post payments.

faqs.q: Which county is Clearfield, Utah in?
faqs.a: Clearfield is in Davis County, and the Davis County treasurer's office in Farmington bills the property tax. The phone number is 801-451-3243.

faqs.q: What is the property tax due date in Clearfield?
faqs.a: Clearfield property tax is due November 30. If November 30 falls on a weekend, the due date moves to the next business day, and penalties start after that day.

faqs.q: What is the Freeport Center in Clearfield?
faqs.a: The Freeport Center is a 680-acre manufacturing and distribution complex on the former Clearfield Naval Supply Depot. It has 78 buildings, about 70 companies and roughly 7,000 workers.

faqs.q: Does Hill Air Force Base affect Clearfield housing?
faqs.a: Yes, the base is next door and is Davis County's largest employer, with nearly 23,000 personnel. Many Clearfield homes are bought and sold by people tied to the base.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clearfield house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses can be sold as they are, with repairs left undone. Tell the buyer about the roof, heating, plumbing and electrical so the terms are clear before closing.
